# Skeletal physics projects the bone chain before resolving world target points

**Draft — native old behavioral RED, production unchanged.** Production source on `main@e89349ca51b4e9d024c194cd3bdf645bd25b6c37`. This concerns root bodies generated by a ragdoll profile, not the parented post-solver writeback in #145. The problem-only Draft preceded the test commit.

1. **Difference.** ZE's [profile spawn](../../../zircon_plugins/physics/runtime/src/skeletal/profile.rs#L271-L335) and [animated drive](../../../zircon_plugins/physics/runtime/src/skeletal/runtime.rs#L149-L191) start with a projected skeleton world TRS and compose successive bone/offset TRS. UE resolves a live bone's world transform before providing it to the body or kinematic target, rather than treating a bone- or component-relative point as the world target. The ZE hierarchy authority is its full affine matrix.
2. **Impact.** Old ZE put a profile-generated root at `(11.107976,0,-4.060660)` instead of `(11.414213,0,-3.707107)` below the sheared skeleton. A nonzero child body offset ended at `(12.414213,0,-3.414214)` both at spawn and when driven, not `(12.414213,0,-2.707107)`, even with a root skeleton entity. On animated release the old velocity was `(2.215952,0,-2.121321) m/s` rather than `(2.828427,0,-1.414214) m/s`; the transition retained the already incorrect last world point.
3. **Cause and Unreal evidence.** [ZE world TRS](../../../zircon_runtime/src/scene/world/derived_state.rs#L450-L462) is a reduction of the true matrix, and [componentwise bone composition](../../../zircon_plugins/physics/runtime/src/skeletal/runtime.rs#L460-L465) cannot carry the shear to a later offset. UE `Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/SkeletalMeshComponentPhysics.cpp:919–928,1071–1084` supplies `GetBoneTransform` to `InitBody`; `Components/SkinnedMeshComponent.cpp:2441–2450,2508–2514` uses the resolved component-to-world transform. The adjacent *matrix* getter (`2391–2432`) composes the bone and component matrices before returning. In `PhysicsEngine/PhysAnim.cpp:683–711` the world bone pose reaches `SetKinematicTarget_AssumesLocked` or `SetGlobalPose_AssumesLocked`; `Experimental/PhysScene_Chaos.cpp:1782–1787` forwards the target. UE's deferred branch resolves the same world pose but currently writes `SetX/SetR` directly (`Experimental/PhysScene_Chaos.cpp:2211–2278`), so not all its animated updates synthesize target velocity. UE also warns on nonuniform scale and approximates body scale (`PhysAnim.cpp:616–622,713–730`); this is not proof that UE physics or `FTransform` supports shear.
4. **Rust direction.** After a genuine old RED, preserve the full matrix while resolving `skeleton_world * bone_chain * body_offset` for the world point. Keep the old rigid rotation and scale policy, as well as the existing bone resolution, topological order and finite checks. Measure linear release from two exact world points; do not reinterpret that as verifying angular velocity or a sheared primitive. Do not change the reverse simulated-pose feed or manually parented body writeback without an independent witness.
5. **Interface and ECS.** [Profile configuration](../../../zircon_plugins/physics/runtime/src/skeletal/profile.rs#L412-L460) uses independent ECS bodies and joint metadata, not scene parenting of bones. [Runtime animated drive](../../../zircon_plugins/physics/runtime/src/runtime_system.rs#L91-L109) precedes the physics step. Validate the real profile and driver in existing unit tests, not a parallel runtime or ABI. Prefab, live solver, ECS hierarchy, public profiles and #145 stay unchanged.
6. **Concrete gate.** Extend the existing skeletal unit test module and preserve its [spawn/control](../../../zircon_plugins/physics/runtime/src/skeletal/tests/cases.rs#L28-L95) and [no-pop/release](../../../zircon_plugins/physics/runtime/src/skeletal/tests/cases.rs#L126-L174) assertions. Port the position-and-velocity observation from local UE HeadlessChaos `EngineInterface.SetKinematicTargetWriteBackEnabled/Disabled` (`Engine/Source/Programs/HeadlessChaos/Private/HeadlessChaosTestPhysicsScene.cpp:1387–1419,1432–1458,1498–1508`). Assert real spawned root points, parent bone vs parent **body offset** distinction, animated drive positions, unchanged last point on release, and `Δworld / Δt` separately. [Four frozen cases](../../../zircon_plugins/physics/runtime/src/skeletal/tests/affine_points.rs) measure scene shear, an independent sheared bone-chain offset at spawn and at drive, and release with two fixed-time samples. The Chaos test is a position/difference oracle, not an assertion that UE's skeletal switch computes release velocity. A direct driver unit test is not a hosted Update or Chaos/Jolt solver run.

**Native Windows/MSVC old `2f53dbee0205703d2d49f503417ca3b89515aff0`:** 2 passed / 4 failed across the exact witnesses and existing controls; all skeletal tests: 26 passed / 4 failed; exit 101 in both. No compile/setup failures. The first external validator mispredicted the numerical result of decomposing a sheared matrix, although the actual tests already reached and failed only the intended coordinate/velocity assertions. Qualification reran the identical SHA-256 native executable with the expected world geometry and a wrong-point margin, not a fixed value for the old TRS approximation. Neither the tests nor production were edited between those invocations.
